title: Auth & Tenant Isolation
objective: After this lesson you will be able to issue JWT sessions with rotation, enforce per-query thread ownership, isolate tenants in data and caches, and prove isolation with negative tests.
why: User B reading user A's threads by guessing IDs is the full-stack nightmare that unit tests miss and attackers find: authorization must live in every data query, not just login. Sessions, ownership predicates, tenant-scoped caches, and negative tests (forbidden access proven refused) form the isolation system — obscurity is not a layer in it.

blocks.text: Access tokens short-lived (minutes), refresh tokens rotating (single-use, theft-detecting via reuse alarms). Secrets server-side only (HttpOnly cookies or memory — never localStorage for tokens). Every authenticated request resolves a principal (user + tenant) that data queries must consume — authentication without per-query authorization is decoration.

blocks.caption: Ownership in every query: predicates, not obscurity

blocks.text: Isolation spans **queries** (owner/tenant predicates), **caches** (tenant in every key — Production Ch.3), **logs** (tenant-tagged, PII-scrubbed), and **errors** (no cross-tenant details in messages). One unscoped layer leaks despite the rest: audits walk all four, per release.

For every read/write path, a test asserting **forbidden access refuses**: cross-user thread read → 403, cross-tenant query → empty-with-audit, expired token → 401. Positive tests prove features; negative tests prove isolation. Untested refusal is hoped refusal.

blocks.title: Enforce ownership
blocks.note: Run it: scoped query, then unauthenticated/missing-tenant refusals, then the cross-read proof. Ownership predicates with negative paths — isolation tested, not trusted.

items: Short JWTs + rotating refresh; secrets never in localStorage; principals consumed per query
Isolation across queries/caches/logs/errors — one unscoped layer leaks despite the rest
Negative tests (403s) prove refusal; untested isolation is hoped isolation

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice ownership checks and map all four outputs. (b) Write the negative test for cross-tenant thread list (userB/tenant2 reading tenant1 data) with expected refusal shape. (c) State the cache-key rule for thread lists with the leak it prevents.
hints: Outputs: scoped-where / unauthenticated / unauthenticated(missing tenant) / cross-read-prevented true.
Negative test: tenant2 principal querying tenant1 thread → 403 + audit entry (refusal with evidence).
Keys: tenant + user + query-signature (personal never shares); prevents cross-tenant cached reads.
exercise.why: Predicate construction (scoped queries), refusal proof (negative tests), and cache isolation (key rules) are the three auth judgments — each verified against attacker-shaped cases.
exercise.code: // Isolation-audit pattern: queries, caches, logs, errors — all four layers.

quiz.q: Thread IDs are unguessable UUIDs; queries unscoped. Secure?
options: No: obscurity is not access control — per-query ownership predicates + negative tests, always
quiz.explain: IDs leak (logs, URLs, referrals). Enforcement lives in query predicates proven by forbidden-access tests.

quiz.q: JWT in localStorage for 'offline mode'. Verdict?
options: XSS-readable secrets without HttpOnly protection: memory/HttpOnly only, PII server-side, storage audited per key
quiz.explain: Browser storage threat model: XSS reads localStorage. Secrets stay out; each stored item justified on record.

quiz.q: Shared cache for thread lists across tenants. Risk + fix?
options: Cross-tenant leakage: tenant+user in every personal key; public content shared with versions only
quiz.explain: Cache keys are access-control rules: personal never shares across tenants. Isolation designed into keys, audited like permissions.

summary: Short sessions, rotating refresh, per-query ownership, four-layer isolation, negative tests proving refusal. Trust predicates, never IDs.
